newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton gain on export quota hopes.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton gain on export quota hopes.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Wednesday bounced back from lower levels as speculators became active buyers on expectations that the government may allow more exports, dealers said.
So far the government has allowed export of 1.22 million bales (170 kg each) of cotton in the current year. Traders says they expect permission for at another 200,000 bales.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 40 rupees to 840/875 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned lifted to 1,450/1,675 rupees per maund from 1,430/1,640 rupees.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) however fell further by 100 rupees to 11,300/11,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) on fresh selling. It was down by 200 rupees on Tuesday.
Overall sentiment remained firm at the close and the market ignored reports that state-owned agencies are planning to cut prices to reduce stock piling.
The Maharashtra Cotton Growers Federation in the western region has already cut prices by 1,000/1,200 rupees per candy for the old crop variety and by 300 rupees per candy for the new crop variety.
